subject: Deployment mode: latency & throughput decision briefing
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Elena Garcia <elena@glossmart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Nov 2027 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Deployment mode: latency & throughput decision briefing

Hi Elena — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and the concrete asks we promised to follow up on so your team can make a deployment-mode decision (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC).

What we heard (from the discovery call):
- Target p99 latency: 45-60ms for short completions (<=128 tokens) for the search/intent pipeline.
- Sustained concurrency: 320 QPS (concurrent requests), peak burst to ~1,200 QPS for 3–5 minutes during batch promotions.
- Requirement: data residency in us-east for production; no on-prem mandate today.
- Primary concern: predictable tail latency during batch promotions and cost for sustained traffic.

High-level recommendation:
- Short-term pilot: Hosted API with a Dedicated capacity pilot for the hottest routes. Hosted can be used for non-critical routes and to speed time-to-value; Dedicated for the latency-sensitive search route to guarantee warm KV caches and reserved GPUs during peak windows.

Next steps I recommend (concrete):
1) Review the attached throughput_matrix.csv (attached) — it maps observed QPS to expected p50/p95/p99 on our Standard Dedicated profile vs Hosted baseline.
2) Schedule a 30-min follow-up with Marissa (solutions lead) and your infra owner Marco to scope a 4-week Dedicated pilot with burst capacity and an autoscale policy.
3) Decide on metrics for the pilot: p99 latency, mean tokens per request, and cost per 1M tokens. We'll instrument traces and per-token cost in Redwood Console.

Proposed tentative dates: pilot start week of Dec 6. If that works, Marissa will share a MAP with milestones.

Attachments: throughput_matrix.csv (CSV, 24KB), glossmart-map.pdf (proposal sketch, 480KB).

Thanks — happy to adjust based on what Marco confirms about nightly batch concurrency.

— Vivek

Thanks, Vivek — this is really helpful. A couple of clarifying questions before we lock dates: 

1) Our p99 SLAs are strict for search (we currently target 100ms p99). Your suggested 45–60ms looks optimistic — is that p99 for a single-token-ish request? What assumptions are in that csv (batching, token length, quantization)?

2) For the burst windows: when you say "burst to ~1,200 QPS," are you assuming sustained GPU warm caches across the burst, or will there be cold-start penalty for new model shards? How much buffer does Dedicated give us vs Hosted?

3) Any suggestion for a lightweight A/B during the pilot so we can measure quality changes if we use a quantized model for cost savings?

If you can send one-page notes on those three points I can share with our infra and procurement leads. Marco, can you confirm if we need VPC-only access (Private) or if dedicated in a public region is acceptable?

— Elena

Subject: Re: Deployment mode: latency & throughput decision briefing

Elena — quick answers inline and attached one-pager (glossmart-map.pdf) with the pilot plan and A/B guidance.

1) About the p99 numbers: the csv assumes short completions (median 45 tokens) and our Standard Dedicated profile with warmed KV cache and continuous batching disabled for the search route (we force single-request fast-path). The p99 figures in the matrix are measured with warmed KV and no batching; the Hosted baseline in the sheet includes typical multi-tenant noise (so tail is higher). If your payloads are much longer than 45 tokens we'll re-run the numbers; also note quantization adds a small deterministic latency delta (2–6ms) but reduces GPU memory footprint which helps density.

2) Burst behavior: Dedicated reserves GPU capacity and keeps KV caches resident; for the duration of the reserved window you should not see cold-start penalties across model shards. Hosted can handle bursts but at higher p99 variance — we surface that in the csv as a 20–40% p99 uplift during noisy multi-tenant peaks. Practically: Dedicated = predictable tail, Hosted = lower operational friction.

3) A/B guidance: run canonical prompts for search on both an FP16 (or int8 quantized) variant and the full-precision variant; capture retrieval accuracy and p99 latency across samples. Our Optimize toolkit can track quality regressions across eval sets and send alerts if scoring drifts >1.5% on your metric. The attached glossmart-map.pdf includes the MAP milestones and evaluation checkpoints.

Proposed follow-up: 30-min call Monday Nov 29 10:00am ET / 7:00am PT with Marissa + your infra lead Marco to finalize pilot SLOs. If that works I'll schedule and include a draft contract stub for Dedicated pilot pricing.

Attachments referenced: throughput_matrix.csv, glossmart-map.pdf.

— Vivek
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Deployment mode: latency & throughput decision briefing

Forwarding a couple of quick ops notes for the pilot (Elena / Marco — adding to the thread so it's in motion):

- Pilot scope: Dedicated pool for search route only. Use Hosted for non-search routes (recommendation to reduce cost).
- Autoscale: configure warm buffer 20% over expected sustained QPS to handle short spikes; set scale-in cooldown at 3 minutes to avoid flapping during promotions.
- Logging & traces: we will enable per-token tracing and token-level cost breakdown in Redwood Console. I will share the Console workspace invite this afternoon.
- Data residency: we can keep production in us-east; if you require a VPC endpoint we'll raise the Private onboarding task but that will add ~3–4 weeks for network validation.

Operational asks from GlossMart for a smooth run: share a representative traffic replay (1–2 days) and a short eval corpus (300 prompts) for quality baselining.

If everyone is aligned I'll open the pilot MAP and draft the Dedicated pilot order; Vivek — please schedule the Nov 29 sync and include Marco's infra contact.

— Marissa
